question: Should OpenClaw core own a versioned aggregate recovery-point contract now, or should the RFC first assign aggregate inventory, obligation, and acceptance-set ownership to the external host lifecycle?
rationale: The implementation is intentionally private and inert until a stacked caller lands, but its identities and fail-closed rules become durable session-state semantics once consumed. Code review cannot safely choose that core-versus-host boundary.

options.title: Approve a narrow core seam
options.body: Accept the aggregate identity as a private OpenClaw contract, name its owner and upgrade rules, and require the first caller to land with focused compatibility proof.

options.title: Pause until RFC ownership is accepted
options.body: Keep this stack open while maintainers settle the core-versus-host boundary, then rebase the implementation onto the accepted contract.

options.title: Keep composition host-owned
options.body: Move the aggregate recovery-point identity and host acceptance semantics out of core, retaining only any smaller snapshot-provider extension that maintainers identify as missing.

recommendation.title: Pause until RFC ownership is accepted
recommendation.body: Keep this stack open while maintainers settle the core-versus-host boundary, then rebase the implementation onto the accepted contract.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged work owns the canonical SQLite-backed agent/session state whose inventory and recovery semantics this proposed contract aggregates.
